verses.1: For the music director. A psalm of David.
verses.2: When the LORD strengthens the king, the king rejoices; when you save him, he exults greatly.
verses.3: You have given him the desire of his heart, and you have not withheld the plea of his lips. Selah.
verses.4: For you have preceded him with blessings of goodness; you have placed on his head a crown of refined gold.
verses.5: He asked for life from you, and you gave it to him—long life, an age of ages.
verses.6: His honor is great through your salvation; you bestow glory and splendor upon him.
verses.7: For you will give him blessings forever; in your presence you will gladden him with joy.
verses.8: For the king has trusted in the LORD; in the steadfast love of the Most High he will not be shaken.
verses.9: May your hand find all his enemies; may your right hand find those who hate him.
verses.10: You will make them like a burning oven at the time of your face—LORD, in your anger you will consume them, and fire will devour them.
verses.11: You will destroy their fruit from the land; you will blot out their descendants from among the children of men.
verses.12: For they plotted evil against you; they devised a scheme that they cannot accomplish.
verses.13: For you will make them the back of the bow; you will prepare their faces in your taut strings.
verses.14: Rise up, LORD, in your might; we will sing and praise your strength.

notes:
Notes
- v. 3: "the plea of his lips" refers to the Greek "δέησις τῶν χειλέων αὐτοῦ" but follows the Hebrew "אֲרֶשֶׁת שְׂפָתָיו" — best read as "the plea of his lips" rather than "the request of his mouth".
- v. 13: "the back of the bow" reflects the Hebrew "שֶׁכֶם בְּמֵיתָרֶיךָ". The metaphor is obscure but likely describes a target aimed at, not a bowstring.
- v. 14: "strength" for גְּבוּרָתֶֽךָ is chosen over "might" to match the poetic tone of the previous chapters.
